reed. The SI has the following objectives: Objective 1: Assessment of existing specification formats and working methods, and requirements for any improvements. Advantages of current tools Shortcomings, pain-points, and potential benefits Requirements Identification Objective 2 (After TSG#109): Taking into account the outcome of objective 1, consider new formats, including but not necessarily limited to plain text format such as Markdown or LaTeX, or another format. Objective 3 (After TSG#109): Taking into account the outcome of objective 1, consider use of Git and ETSI FORGE database to store specifications and manage version control. Other alternatives are not precluded. As part of the study, trial TSs and CRs will be created, to evaluate the considered formats and processes and their applicability to the different working groups across 3GPP. Findings, conclusions, and recommendations will be recorded in TR 21.802. In parallel, in various RAN groups the discussion on the future of 3GPP specification was triggered and tests are currently ongoing. RAN5 also have an ongoing offline discussion on the dedicated email thread. To ensure the RAN5 relevant aspects are considered, RAN5 leadership team decided to form a group of RAN5 representatives to actively participate in the conference calls throughout the activity. In this document we provide status update for the 6G spec modernization activity. We also highlight RAN5 aspects related to this activity.

Athens, Greece, 17th - 21st February, 2025 Agenda item: 4.2.4 Document for: Discussion and Endorsement Introduction This contribution intends to suggest a recommendation/guidance to be provided by RAN5 leadership in order to reduce the number of overall CRs treated during each meeting. Discussion Treatment of discussion paper but especially CRs is a time-intensive task for various parties involved: MCC: implementation of CRs into specs once agreed RAN5 chairs/vice chairs/convenors/secretaries/assistants: tracking/revising CRs in the respective spreadsheets and databases Delegates: review/discussion/tracking of CRs internally (meeting preparation) and tracking of CRs during the meeting It is therefore in everyone’s best interest to limit the number of contributions and CRs as much as possible. In RAN4, the RAN4 leadership has formally enforced the number of contributions (discussion, LS, simulations, draft CR/TPs, etc.) for a number of years already [1] and is reminding delegates in their ‘RAN4#X meeting Arrangements and Guidelines’ document every meeting, e.g., RAN5 obviously has their agenda and TDoc reservation setup very differently than RAN4, e.g., the same spec can be discussed in vastly different agenda items/WIs and different sub-agenda items can be assigned to different clauses of the same spec. In order to optimize the handling of contributions, it is suggested for RAN5 leadership to periodically provide a recommendation to the group to encourage each company to limit the number of contributions (discussion papers and CRs) and/or consolidate TDocs for each agenda item to reduce the number of contributions. Especially, editorial and RAN4 alignment CRs submitted per agenda by each company item should be combined to avoid multiple CRs in the same agenda item. Whether this guidance should be captured in a PRD, e.g., PRD18 (“General processes and practices”), could be discussed separately. We realize that there are exceptions and sometimes separate CRs to a TR/TS might be needed, e.g., essential corrections. Proposal 1: RAN5 leadership to periodically provide a recommendation to the group for each company to limit the number of contributions (discussion papers and CRs) and/or consolidate TDocs for each agenda item to reduce the number of contributions Proposal 2: RAN5 leadership to provide a guidance to the group to make sure that companies combine editorial and RAN4 alignment CRs submitted per agenda item to avoid multiple CRs with similar/same intent in the same agenda item. Conclusion The following observations and conclusions were made in this contribution. Proposal 1: RAN5 leadership to periodically provide a recommendation to the group for each company to limit the number of contributions (discussion papers and CRs) and/or consolidate TDocs for each agenda item to reduce the number of contributions Proposal 2: RAN5 leadership to provide a guidance to the group to make sure that companies combine editorial and RAN4 alignment CRs submitted per agenda item to avoid multiple CRs with similar/same intent in the same agenda item. R4-2114691, RAN4 Meeting Efficiency Improvements, RAN4 leadership, 3GPP TSG-RAN WG4 Meeting #100-e, August 2021 [Tables] Table 1: For each individual agenda of all WI/SI-s, the limit of submitted tdoc follows the principle in RAN4 Meeting Efficiency Improvements (R4-2114691) Maximum one discussion paper per lowest level agenda item (AI) per company/organization in principle.

ge 1) will have a lot in common, especially: Minimum requirements Test configuration table (test points) Test requirements Annex A (RMC) Annex B (Propagation conditions), Annex C (DL signal levels), Annex D (Interference), Annex E (EVM definition), Annex F (test tolerance), Annex G (test time), Annex H (signal levels) It is expected that the overlap/duplication between 38.521-1 and 38.521-2 is not as high due to NR range 1 likely being conducted tests and NR range 2 being OTA tests. Proposal 1: For RAN5 to follow the same specification structure as RAN4, and to follow the same clause numbering as the RAN4 specs. Proposal 2: For RAN5 to consider the different spec structure options and identify additional pros and cons coming from a RAN5 perspective. Proposal 3: To inform RAN4 about the outcome so that a spec structure optimized for both WGs can be selected.

Bullet b) and c), of Observation 2 is not intentional, but consequence of negligence. Observation 5: Some inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs for requirements of spurious emission for UE co-existence are not intentional, but consequence of negligence. With more and more Releases coming up, the inconsistencies will be more and more serious as it is too easy to forget to update the specs of all the previous Releases (e.g., It is not easy for delegates to submit 11 LTE correction CRs from Rel-8 to Rel-18 simultaneously). The inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs also exists for other requirements, e.g., MOP, OoBB, Narrow band blocking and etc, and RAN5 spec does not consider the inconsistencies for other requirements except spurious emission for UE co-existence.

6.521-2 for LTE RRM test cases in sections 4–8 of TS 36.521-3 to permit waiving the FDD test cases if the corresponding TDD test cases are executed. The priority order is: TDD-TDD > FDD-TDD > HF-FDD > TDD-FDD > FDD-FDD. For example： In the 5G RRM specs TS 38.133 V19.4.0 (March 2026) [2] and TS 38.533 V19.2.0 (March 2026) [3], all test cases except those listed in the table below include an identical note clarifying that the UE shall only be tested under one of the supported test configurations. There are 9 test cases without such a note in both RAN4 and RAN5 specs (highlighted in Orange); 5 test cases with this note in RAN4 spec but not in RAN5 spec (highlighted in Yellow); and 4 test cases with the note in RAN5 spec but not in RAN4 spec (highlighted in Green). Table 1：Test cases without Note. Observation 6: In TS 38.133 V19.4.0 (2026-03) [2] and TS 38.533 V19.2.0 (2026-03) [3], the majority of test cases include a NOTE indicating that "The UE is only required to be tested in one of the supported test configurations." However, the following exceptions are identified: Nine test cases lack this NOTE in both RAN4 and RAN5 specs (highlighted in Orange); Five test cases include this NOTE in RAN4 spec but not in RAN5 spec (highlighted in Yellow); Four test cases lack this NOTE in RAN4 spec but include it in RAN5 spec (highlighted in Green). Observation 7: The five test cases highlighted in Yellow are not Measurement Performance Requirement-related test cases. Proposal 5：Revise TS 38.533 to align with TS 38.133 for the five test cases highlighted in Yellow. Proposal 6a: For the eight non-Measurement Performance Requirement-related test cases that lack the NOTE in RAN4 spec (highlighted in Orange and Green with black font in Table 1), a CR shall be submitted to RAN4 to introduce the NOTE. For the five test cases highlighted in Orange with black font in Table 1, TS 38.533 shall be revised with RAN4 dependency. Proposal 6b: Following the approach taken for the four green-highlighted test cases, revise TS 38.533 independently of RAN4 to introduce the NOTE for the five orange-highlighted black-font test cases in Table 1. The test cases in red font in the table above are Measurement Performance Requirement test cases. The majority of Measurement Performance Requirement test cases in both RAN4 and RAN5 5G RRM specs already include this NOTE, including test cases in TS 38.533 sections 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.7 and 8.5.2 which shall be dependent on the NR band of the target cell as specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. Observation 8: The majority of Measurement Performance Requirement test cases in both RAN4 and RAN5 5G RRM specs include a NOTE indicating that "The UE is only required to be tested in one of the supported test configurations", including test cases in TS 38.533 sections 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.7 and 8.5.2 which shall be dependent on the NR band of the target cell as specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. However, there are exceptions: Five such test cases lack this NOTE in RAN4 spec; Four such test cases lack this NOTE in RAN5 spec; One such test case lacks this NOTE in RAN4 spec but includes it in RAN5 spec. According to GCF Conformance Assessment Table 3.101.0_20260508_r004 [1], all GCF LTE RRM test cases related to Measurement Performance Requirements are from TS 36.521‑3 section 9 and shall be tested on all supported bands (i.e., all supported FDD bands and all supported TDD bands), which is consistent with TS 36.521‑3 clause 3A.3.4. However, for 5G RRM—as shown in the table below—some Measurement Performance Requirement test cases require testing on all supported bands, while others only require testing on a single band (either one FDD band or one TDD band). Observation 9: According to GCF Conformance Assessment Table 3.101.0_2026

ate the “Number of TC Executions” column in TS 36.521-2 for LTE RRM test cases in sections 4–8 of TS 36.521-3 to permit testing in only one of the following configurations: TDD-TDD, FDD-TDD, HD-FDD, TDD-FDD, or FDD-FDD. For example： In the 5G RRM specs TS 38.133 V19.4.0 (March 2026) [2] and TS 38.533 V19.2.0 (March 2026) [3], all test cases except those listed in the table below include an identical note clarifying that the UE shall only be tested under one of the supported test configurations. There are 9 test cases without such a note in both RAN4 and RAN5 specs (highlighted in Orange); 5 test cases with this note in RAN4 spec but not in RAN5 spec (highlighted in Yellow); and 4 test cases with the note in RAN5 spec but not in RAN4 spec (highlighted in Green). Table 1：Test cases without Note. Observation 6: In TS 38.133 V19.4.0 (2026-03) [2] and TS 38.533 V19.2.0 (2026-03) [3], the majority of test cases include a NOTE indicating that "The UE is only required to be tested in one of the supported test configurations." However, the following exceptions are identified: Nine test cases lack this NOTE in both RAN4 and RAN5 specs (highlighted in Orange); Five test cases include this NOTE in RAN4 spec but not in RAN5 spec (highlighted in Yellow); Four test cases lack this NOTE in RAN4 spec but include it in RAN5 spec (highlighted in Green). Observation 7: The five test cases highlighted in Yellow are not Measurement Performance Requirement-related test cases. Proposal 5：Revise TS 38.533 to align with TS 38.133 for the five test cases highlighted in Yellow. Proposal 6a: For the eight non-Measurement Performance Requirement-related test cases that lack the NOTE in RAN4 spec (highlighted in Orange and Green with black font in Table 1), a CR shall be submitted to RAN4 to introduce the NOTE. For the five test cases highlighted in Orange with black font in Table 1, TS 38.533 shall be revised with RAN4 dependency. Proposal 6b: Following the approach taken for the four green-highlighted test cases, revise TS 38.533 independently of RAN4 to introduce the NOTE for the five orange-highlighted black-font test cases in Table 1. The test cases in red font in the table above are Measurement Performance Requirement test cases. The majority of Measurement Performance Requirement test cases in both RAN4 and RAN5 5G RRM specs already include this NOTE, including test cases in TS 38.533 sections 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.7 and 8.5.2 which shall be dependent on the NR band of the target cell as specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. Observation 8: The majority of Measurement Performance Requirement test cases in both RAN4 and RAN5 5G RRM specs include a NOTE indicating that "The UE is only required to be tested in one of the supported test configurations", including test cases in TS 38.533 sections 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.7 and 8.5.2 which shall be dependent on the NR band of the target cell as specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. However, there are exceptions: Five such test cases lack this NOTE in RAN4 spec; Four such test cases lack this NOTE in RAN5 spec; One such test case lacks this NOTE in RAN4 spec but includes it in RAN5 spec. According to GCF Conformance Assessment Table 3.101.0_20260508_r004 [1], all GCF LTE RRM test cases related to Measurement Performance Requirements are from TS 36.521‑3 section 9 and shall be tested on all supported bands (i.e., all supported FDD bands and all supported TDD bands), which is consistent with TS 36.521‑3 clause 3A.3.4. However, for 5G RRM—as shown in the table below—some Measurement Performance Requirement test cases require testing on all supported bands, while others only require testing on a single band (either one FDD band or one TDD band). Observation 9: According to GCF Conformance Assessment Table 3.101.0_20260

rses one of the following proposals list below Proposal 2.1: To define version controlled Rel-16 NR test specs as per RAN4s DRAFT Rel-16 core specs-- both Rel-15 and Rel-16 NR test specs will be maintained simultaneously. Pros: To fulfill the requirements from industry to the greatest extent. Cons: RAN5 never maintain any version controlled RAN5 specs as per the DRAFT core spec and RAN5 does NOT have different spec versions for different releases, all core spec release contents go into the same test spec, and the test spec version corresponds to the latest core spec version that test spec is derived from. Proposal 2.3: Only to prepare and endorse Rel-16 CRs basing on Rel-15 test specs during the 2 RAN5 meetings of RAN5#4 Ad-hoc@April and RAN5#83@May. No draft Rel-16 test specs in RAN5. All the RAN5 agreed Rel-16 CRs will be submitted to RP#84@June together with RAN4 Rel-16 CRs for approval. The corresponding RAN5 test specs will be raised from Rel-15 to Rel-16 (as RAN5 is only maintaining one version in the traditional practice). MCC need to implement at first all RAN #84 approved Rel-15 CRs into 15.x.x, then MCC will take this 15.x.x version and implement all Rel-16 CRs to make a 16.x.x. Proposal 2.4: To define Rel-16 TR(s) to capture all the required Rel-16 content (delta vs Rel-15 RAN5 TSs) until the RAN4 Rel-16 TSs have been approved. Proposal 3: RAN5#5 5G-NR Adhoc@April and RAN5#83@May meetings shall only handle CRs covering Rel-16 NR CA/DC Band Combinations that have 100% core part completed by RAN4#90@Feb. RAN5 should have visibility to the status of individual Rel-16 NR CA/DC band combinations after RAN4#90@Feb. through the WI Status Reports submitted to RP#83@March. Discussion: Decision: The document was revised to R5-190618. ystems. UE shall consider the spurious emission of all protected bands included in the latest Version of spec at the stage of its design. It is up to certification organization to decide which Version of spec can be accepted for UE certification. Observation 5: Some inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs for requirements of spurious emission for UE co-existence are not intentional, but consequence of negligence. With more and more Releases coming up, the inconsistencies will be more and more serious as it is too easy to forget to update the specs of all the previous Releases (e.g., It is not easy for delegates to submit 11 LTE correction CRs from Rel-8 to Rel-18 simultaneously). Proposal 2: RAN5 shall take the latest Release of RAN4 spec as reference for the requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence and remove the Release information in minimum requirements and test requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence. New bands/new CBWs/or new PCs introduced to later Releases can be excluded if there is no interested operator in RAN5. Proposal 3: Minimum requirements and test requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence in TS 38.521-1/-2/-3 and TS 36.521-1 shall be updated as per Proposal 1 and Proposal 2.
